notes: Main disagreements: (1) phase, mostly general vs course-start/before-course/during-work for quoted example rationales and for the sentence "best handled by proactive teaching" (resolved by whether the passage states a principle, which is general, or a time-bound action; the cancellation of Turnitin AI detection and similar facts became when-misuse or general); (2) actor on factual or explanatory sentences (all vs student/instructor/admin), resolved by whom the sentence addresses or who acts, with no-addressee facts coded all; (3) modality: "expects", "an expectation", "critical that", "please remember" coded should, "potentially" coded may, "they must submit a report" coded must, and "should be mindful" coded should rather than should-not; (4) policy_type: causes of dishonesty (P68 vs P99, made P99), the 33% Review Board statistic (P55 vs P39, made P39), additional-policy preference (P04 vs P02, kept P04), peer-R1 benchmark (P88, remapped to P39 with fit_note); (5) unit_stance on unauthorized-use classification (prohibit vs restrict, made restrict) and on attribution (permit, made require). Coder B coded more: quoted instructor examples in the provost memo (kept with fit_notes that they are examples), the detector-rationale facts, and the written reporting steps; all real and kept (9 B-only). A-only: 4 real facts/expectations kept; one general academic-integrity sentence on the CCS page (faculty must clarify expectations) dropped as not AI-specific.
